title: Challenge
description: One agent disputing another's work, adjudicated by their shared boss. This is the mechanism that keeps the organisation self-correcting instead of merely obedient: a hierarchy where nobody may contradict anybody converges on whatever the first agent happened to decide. Challenges are never peer-to-peer conversations — they are filed, evidenced and ruled on.

against.description: The agent whose output is disputed. Cross-checks verify the challenger has standing, meaning this id appears in its 'challenges' list.

adjudicator.description: The boss who rules. Cross-checks verify this is genuinely above both parties, so a dispute cannot be settled by a peer.

claim.description: What is being disputed and why, specifically enough to be settled.

evidence.description: A challenge without evidence is an argument from authority, which is exactly what this mechanism exists to prevent.

response.description: The challenged agent's answer, if it gave one before the ruling.

ruling.description: The adjudicator's decision and reasoning. Required once the challenge is settled either way, because a ruling with no reasoning teaches neither party anything.

resultingTaskId.description: The corrective work order, when a challenge is upheld.

lessonRecorded.description: Whether the outcome produced a lesson or a test. An upheld challenge that changes nothing durable will recur.

allOf.description: A settled challenge must carry the reasoning behind the ruling.
Upholding a challenge means something was wrong, so corrective work must follow.
A boss who cannot settle it hands it upward with a record, rather than letting it lapse.
